slice: exploring: a body's selves meeting change, with no fighters apart

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: Nearly each cell with a nucleus shows on its surface short pieces, mostly 8 to 10 amino acids long, of the proteins it is making within; a passing cytotoxic T cell whose receptor matches a piece foreign to the body, a virus's for one, recognizes and kills that cell, and a cell showing too little of these pieces meets a natural killer cell's attack. Each cell is sharing its own interior's parity across, and a passing cell observes it from its own side.

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: Skin epithelial stem cells keep a memory of an earlier inflammation, up to six months in mice: the inflammation opens sites in their chromatin and some stay open, and a later wound in that skin closes more than twice as fast, the stem cells moving into it more effectively: a memory of inflammation in skin stem cells.

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: Macrophages in the heart's atrioventricular node express connexin-43 and touch heart muscle cells directly, as electron microscopy shows; deleting their connexin-43 impairs the node's conduction, and depleting macrophages and other myeloid cells brings a first-degree block within 24 hours, progressing to complete heart block, the last of three degrees: cells a field calls immune take part in the heart's own conduction.

One theory, discontinuity theory, reads immunity this way: an immune response comes with the speed of change in the molecular motifs a tissue shows to immune receptors, not with a thing's origin; a persistent or slowly appearing motif meets tolerance in its reading, microbes that arrive early and persist among them, and a sudden change, even in a body's own fast-growing tumour, meets a response in its reading.

An immune system of fighter cells apart from other cells is a field's explaining: nearly each cell with a nucleus shows pieces of its own interior on its surface, skin stem cells keep a memory of an earlier inflammation, heart macrophages take part in the node's conduction, and one theory reads a body's response by the speed of change; by that reading, immunity is a body's same-existing-society observing change beside its prior with each of its selves, a defending and a fighting being a field's words.

items.section: 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone
items.sentence: A same-existing-society orients as one surface, and its orienting is in no self alone: social abundancing.
items.text: Within one body a same-existing-society discovers: nearly each cell with a nucleus shows pieces of its own making on its surface, a passing cytotoxic T cell whose receptor matches a foreign piece recognizes and kills that cell, and among B cells competing in a germinal centre, higher-affinity antibodies to a shape new to the body arise over time, in no cell alone.
